text:
olivia: @channel Seeing repeated 504s for tenant AcmeCorp on hosted API since 09:12 UTC. Customers report p95 ~12s then 504. example req id req_0a1b2c. Enqueue delays visible in logs. https://grafana.redwood/tenant/AcmeCorp

sam: On it — can you paste a sample request payload + exact timestamp?

olivia: payload: {"model":"redwood-4-large","input_length":4500,"prompt":"..."} request ts 2024-11-02T09:12:05Z. Many requests are long (>4k tokens). continuous-batching backlog metrics spiking. sample error: `ERROR gateway: request timed out after 6000ms -> 504`

devon: Seeing same traces: `queue_depth` hitting configured max 256 on batcher pool cp-uk-west-2-3. KV-cache misses are high. metric `cbatch_pending` climbed to ~320.

luis: paste logs snippet pls

olivia: logs:
```
2024-11-02T09:12:05Z INFO enqueue req=req_0a1b2c queue_pos=250
2024-11-02T09:12:12Z WARN dequeue delayed req=req_0a1b2c wait_ms=7100
2024-11-02T09:12:12Z ERROR handler timeout req=req_0a1b2c status=504
```

maria: looks like customer payloads include long sequences and streaming disabled — that increases per-request runtime in the serving engine.

sam: repro steps?

olivia: quick repro curl to hosted endpoint (token redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-4-large","input":"<~4k tokens>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

devon: hypothesis: continuous-batcher backlog + queue depth cap -> early 504s. Requests sit in queue longer than gateway handler timeout. KV-cache coldstarts for long sequences slow dequeues too.

luis: immediate mitigations we can try:
- increase batcher `queue_depth` from 256 -> 512 on affected pool
- temporarily enforce ingress ACL to cap max tokens per request for AcmeCorp to 2000
- enable optimistic dequeue / smaller batch sizes for that pool
- failover tenant to smaller model variant `redwood-4-medium`

maria: any risks to increasing queue depth? might increase memory usage & KV churn, could postpone failures but increase pod pressure.

sam: plan: 1) apply tenant rate-limit to block new ultra-long requests; 2) failover existing tenant traffic to medium; 3) monitor and then cautiously bump queue_depth if needed.

opsbot: deploybot: rolling update scheduled to batcher pool cp-uk-west-2-3: set queue_depth=512 (dry-run) by sam at 09:27 UTC

devon: after applying rate-limit + failover, observed p95 improved from ~12s -> ~800ms and error rate dropped to 0.8% (was ~9%). dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/CBatcher

olivia: customer acknowledges degraded but usable. keeping them on medium until we tune kv-cache and batching params.

luis: follow-ups:
- run load-profile test with many long sequences to tune `continuous_batch_max_wait_ms` and `batch_size_limits`
- add eviction policy adjustment to prioritize short/streaming requests during spikes
- add automated tenant throttle when `cbatch_pending` > 200 (circuit-breaker)

maria: I'll spin up a postmortem doc and assign action items (owner: devon for tests, luis for config changes, sam for runbook update).

olivia: creating support ticket with mitigations + customer note. ticket #SUP-12458

sam: operational note: I did a targeted restart of the most memory-starved batcher pod after confirming queue_length > 400 and memory > 85% via `kubectl exec` and `top`.

devon: root cause summary: tenant spike comprised of many long-sequence requests -> CBatcher backlog + KV-cache coldstarts -> batcher queue_depth cap reached -> requests queued past gateway handler timeout -> 504s. mitigated by tenant rate-limit + fallback to smaller model. next: automated throttles + config tuning + add early-detection alert on cbatch_pending growth.

maria: cc @oncall — planning a config-change window tomorrow 02:00 UTC to deploy throttles and run load tests.

olivia: closing thread for now. will reopen if we see recurrence. thanks all :thumbsup:
